g.text: Failover groups — configure, hide, walk, stick
a child epgState is never null
partial index {source, failoverGroupId} · written only by the group routes
Export surface — a group is one line
children stay badged in the UI — never in the .m3u or the guide
2 · PLAY-TIME WALK — RUST DATA PLANE + NODE RESOLVE SEAM
resolve failed — dead scrape · expired auth · unknown adapter
transport failure after the RSL retry budget (502 / 503 / 504 · timeouts)
definitive 4xx / 5xx — only when failoverOnDefiniteError is on (default off)
0 = the channel itself · N ≥ 1 = its Nth Active child
fetch failed → retry the cursor (fresh resolve · mirror rotation)
resolve failed → start one past the cursor
first try keeps the full RSL budget (retry + backoff)
later candidates: one shot, no backoff — beat the player timeout
children: role child · status Active · sort failoverOrder
200 · grant — policySource = the child's own adapter
502 · resolve_failed — this candidate died, try the next
410 · failover_exhausted — nothing left, end the walk
pin the cursor to this attempt
serve under the parent's URL + identity
knob on → stash it and walk on
else reset cursor → 502 to the player
only an attempt that SERVED 2xx keeps the pin
every other exit resets the cursor to 0
FAILOVER_CURSOR_IDLE — 300s idle → back to the parent
hops inherit the pinned candidate's policy_key
a live session never snaps back to the dead parent
attribution stays on the parent's (source, entry)
cleared on attempt 0 · pruned with the session
Node names the parent · Rust carries the session rid

svg.text: Failover can never mask a dead parent: the scheduled probe keeps probing hidden children, and probeAll resolves each channel itself (no attempt).
